statement.excerpt: I stressed the same in my Senate testimony, but nothing thus far in existing US law addresses this need.
statement.document_title: Scoop: What former employees of OpenAI are worried about

companies should not be able to make decisions of potentially enormous magnitude on their own

our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading concerns external oversight of consequential frontier AI development and release decisions.
A qualifying law must give an external body meaningful influence over those company decisions. Merely advising the government or regulating particular downstream uses does not necessarily qualify.
US law includes federal and state law; the speaker did not expressly restrict the claim to federal statutes.
Because this describes existing law without a reporting period, the target is the legal position on the publication date, August 23, 2024.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive review of applicable federal and state law establishes that no law then provided the described external oversight.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An applicable law in force on August 23, 2024 gave an external body meaningful authority over consequential frontier AI company decisions and their risks and benefits.
